The mechanism is real and verifiable in the diff; it should use response.ok or response.status.

judged_text: Success is checked via `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of response.ok; under HTTP/2 (or proxies) statusText is empty, and Salesforce may return lowercase "ok", so the check throws HttpError 400 on a successful refresh or accepts based on a non-normative field. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh-token fetch checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` instead of using `response.ok` / `response.status`. This is diff-grounded and can misclassify successful responses when `statusText` is empty or non-standard, causing erroneous 400s, and can also allow non-2xx responses through if `statusText` happens to be "OK".
